Governing theory established and recorded: every S-number is n=m^2 for root m, so T(N)=sum over m in [2,isqrt(N)] of m^2*[S(m)] — the root reduction turning N candidates into sqrt(N). The general multi-block class (OEIS A104113/A038206) has no closed form beyond the mod-9 filter (m^2≡m mod 9, i.e. m≡0 or 1 mod 9); the two-block Kaprekar/torn-number subcase is parametrised (Iannucci unitary-divisor formula) but is a proper subset. All recorded in CONTEXT.md Established and as source-backed claims (a038206-*, partition-sum-invariant-mod9, dudeney-torn-number-two-block, iannucci-kaprekar-divisor-formula).

Derivation written to /workspace/solution.md: the root-reduction identity T(N)=sum_{2<=m<=isqrt(N)} m^2*[S(m)], why it applies (each S-number is determined by its square root, m>=2) and what it reduces the work to (10^12 candidates down to 10^6 roots). The mod-9 filter prunes 7/9 of roots. This is the method the three candidate implementations branch from.
